COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
UKHC010142122026
WPCRL/1605/2026
Satyam Pundir
--Petitioner
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand
--Respondent
Hon’ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey, Advocate for 
the petitioner. 
Mr. Dinesh Chauhan and Mr. Pramod 
Tewari, A.G.A. for the State of Uttarakhand. 
2. It has come on record that Dinesh Chandra 
expired on 24.12.2024, whereas the alleged gift 
deed was executed on 20.12.2025, i.e. nearly one 
year after his death. Despite this, the said gift 
deed purports to have been executed by Dinesh 
Chandra himself. It is, therefore, prima facie 
evident that the gift deed could not have been 
executed by Dinesh Chandra. It is further 
surprising that the petitioner, in whose favour the 
alleged gift deed was executed, has alone been 
arrayed as an accused, whereas neither the 
attesting witnesses to the gift deed nor any other 
person associated with its execution has, so far, 
been made an accused.
3. On the previous occasion, learned State 
Counsel was directed to obtain specific 
instructions as to why the F.I.R. has been 
registered against the petitioner alone and as to 
what steps have been taken during the course of 
investigation against the other persons who were 
connected with or witnessed the execution of the 
alleged gift deed. Today, on the basis of written 
instructions, learned State Counsel submits that 
the investigation is still in progress and that,  surprisingly, till date, the statement of no person 
has been recorded by the Investigating Officer.
4. Having perused the record, this Court finds 
that the facts emerging on record raise serious 
questions regarding the authenticity and manner 
of execution of the alleged gift deed. Since Dinesh 
Chandra had already expired on 24.12.2024, the 
execution of the gift deed dated 20.12.2025, 
purportedly by him, prima facie indicates that 
some other person may have impersonated 
Dinesh Chandra and executed the said 
document. The role of the persons who were 
present at and attested the execution of the 
registered gift deed, particularly the two witnesses 
who purportedly identified the executant as 
Dinesh Chandra, also requires proper 
investigation. It is further significant that the 
alleged gift deed is a registered document and 
was executed before the Sub-Registrar, 
Dehradun. The process of registration ordinarily 
involves taking photographs of the executant at 
the time of registration. The Investigating Officer 
ought to have collected the relevant registration 
record, including the photograph(s) taken at the 
office of the Sub-Registrar, and compared the 
same with the photograph of Dinesh Chandra 
available on the registered gift deed and/or with 
other authenticated photographs or identity 
documents of the deceased. The failure to 
undertake such basic and material investigative 
steps, coupled with the fact that no statement 
has yet been recorded, prima facie reflects a 
serious lapse in the investigation.
5. Learned State Counsel is directed to file 
counter affidavit, within a period of two weeks.
6. List on 11.09.2026.
 (Alok Mahra, J.) 
 19.08.2026
Arpan

Satyam Pundir
--Petitioner
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand
--Respondent
Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey, Advocate for 
the petitioner.
2. Mr. Jai Prakash, A.G.A. for the State.
3. By means of the present writ petition, 
petitioner seeks quashing of FIR No. 156 of 2026, 
under Sections 318(4), 336(3), 338, 340(2) of 
BNS, registered at Police Station- Basant Vihar, 
District Dehradun.
4. In the FIR, it is averred that forged gift deed 
was executed of the land belonging to the late 
father of the complainant. In the said gift deed, 
some other person had impersonated himself to 
be the father of the complainant. The said gift 
deed was executed on 20.12.2025 whereas father 
of the complainant died on 24.12.2024.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits 
that only petitioner has been named as an 
accused in the FIR; that this property was 
purchased by the petitioner on the advice of the 
property dealer; that the petitioner never knew 
the father of the complainant nor any other party 
and he paid consideration of more than Rs. 1 
Crore to the executants through cash and bank 
transactions. On this basis, it is submitted that 
he himself has been cheated by the said persons. 6. On the last occasion, this Court directed 
that detail investigation be carried out in respect 
of other person, who appeared before the 
Registrar and impersonated himself as father of 
the complainant. On instructions, learned State 
Counsel submits that investigation in that regard 
is underway.
7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and 
perused the record.
8. Be that as it may, since the petitioner is a 
bonafide purchaser of the property and only to 
save some stamp duty, on the advice of property 
dealer, the gift deed was executed in place of sale 
deed, therefore, this Court finds some substance 
in the submission made by learned counsel for 
the petitioner and having considered the 
submissions, this Court is of the view that this 
matter definitely requires deliberation.
9. Issue notice to respondent no. 3, returnable 
within four weeks. Steps to be taken within a 
week.
10. List after service report is received.
11. Meanwhile, counter-affidavit be filed by the 
respondents.
12. Till the next date of listing, as an interim 
measure, petitioner shall not be arrested in 
relation to the aforesaid FIR, provided, he co￾operates with the investigation.
13. Stay Application made therefor stands 
disposed of accordingly.
 (Alok Mahra J.) 03.09.2026
Ujjwal

Satyam Pundir

 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand
--Respondent
Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey, learned 
counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. Deepak Bisht, learned Deputy 
A.G. along with Mr. Akshay Latwal, learned 
A.G.A. for the State.
3. Mr. Bhuwan Bhatt, learned counsel 
for respondent no.3.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner 
would submit that the petitioner has filed 
an amendment application; however, 
inadvertently, the offences which have 
been added during the course of 
investigation under Sections 3(1)(f) and 
3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and the 
Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) 
Act, 1989, for which the amendment 
application has been filed, have wrongly 
been mentioned as Sections 3(2)(b). He, 
therefore, prays that the petitioner may be 
permitted to carry out the necessary 
correction in the amendment application in  the Court.
5. Learned State counsel as well as 
learned counsel for respondent no.2 do not 
dispute the aforesaid submission.
6. Accordingly, the petitioner is 
permitted to carry out the necessary 
correction in the amendment application in 
the Court.
7. For the reasons stated, the 
amendment application is allowed.
8. Let amended memo be filed by 
Monday i.e. on 21.09.2026.
9. List this case on 26.10.2026.
10. Learned counsel for the respondent 
no.2 may file counter affidavit in the 
meantime.
11. Interim order dated 03.09.2026 to 
continue till the next date of listing.
(Alok Mahra, J.)
 18-09-2026
Mamta
